newsitem.title: ALGERIA: Forces kill two guerrillas in Algiers - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: Forces kill two guerrillas in Algiers - newspaper.

text.p: Algerian security forces killed two Moslem guerrillas and destroyed five rebel hideouts in Bainem forest on the heights of Algiers, said Le Matin newspaper on Tuesday.
"The huge amount of ammunition recovered by security forces suggests that about 30 terrorists have been hidden there," said Le Matin.
The newspaper said Bainem forest is used by Moslem rebels as a transit hideout for guerrillas to rest before and after their attacks in the Algerian capital.

Government forces raided the hideouts in Bainem on Sunday night, three days after Algeria's general election in which President Liamine Zeroual's supporters emerged as the main political force with 155 seats in the 380-member National Assembly (lower house).
About 60,000 people have died in Algeria's violence since early 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a huge lead.
Moderate legal Islamists won 103 seats in the assembly. The outlawed radical Islamic Salvation Front (FIS) was barred from taking part in the poll.
